questions.explanation: Condensation releases heat energy into the surroundings as water vapour changes into liquid droplets, unlike melting, evaporation, and sublimation, which all absorb heat energy.

questions.topic: States of Water and Changes of State
questions.question: Which of these is the best everyday example of condensation?
options: Water droplets forming on the outside of a cold glass of juice on a warm day
An ice cube melting on a countertop
A puddle drying up in the sun
Water boiling in a kettle
questions.explanation: Water droplets forming on the outside of a cold glass on a warm day is a classic everyday example of condensation, where water vapour in the air cools and turns back into liquid.

questions.question: Which of these best describes why water is described as having 'no fixed shape' in its liquid state?
options: It takes the shape of whatever container holds it
It always stays in a perfect cube shape
It always stays in a perfect sphere shape
It has a permanent shape that never changes
questions.explanation: Liquid water has no fixed shape of its own — it takes the shape of whatever container holds it, while still keeping a fixed volume.

questions.question: Water has a fixed volume in its liquid state, even though it does not have a fixed shape.
questions.explanation: Liquid water has a fixed volume — it does not compress or expand to fill any given space — even though it takes the shape of its container.

questions.question: Which of these best explains why the water cycle is powered mainly by the Sun's energy?
options: Solar heat drives evaporation from oceans, lakes, and rivers, starting the cycle
The Sun has no role in the water cycle at all
The water cycle is powered entirely by wind, not heat
The Sun only affects precipitation, not evaporation
questions.explanation: The water cycle is mainly powered by the Sun's heat energy, which drives evaporation from oceans, lakes, and rivers, starting the overall cycle.

questions.question: During a long drought, a region's rivers and lakes shrink noticeably. Which explanation best fits the water cycle concept?
options: Evaporation and usage are removing water faster than precipitation is replenishing it in that region
Rivers and lakes always stay exactly the same size regardless of weather
Droughts always increase the amount of water in rivers and lakes
The water cycle stops completely during a drought
questions.explanation: During a drought, evaporation and water usage remove water from rivers and lakes faster than precipitation replenishes it, causing them to shrink — a real-world imbalance in local water cycle stages.

questions.question: Which of these best explains why doctors and scientists sometimes use saline (saltwater) solutions in medicine?
options: Water's solvent property allows salts and other substances to be dissolved at controlled, useful concentrations
Saltwater cannot be used safely for any medical purpose
Salt always makes water unsafe to use in any way
Water cannot dissolve salt at all
questions.explanation: Water's solvent property allows salts to be dissolved at controlled, safe concentrations, which is why saline (saltwater) solutions have medical uses.

questions.question: Not all liquids are equally good solvents; water is unusually effective at dissolving a wide variety of substances compared to many other liquids.
questions.explanation: Water is unusually effective at dissolving a wide variety of substances compared to many other common liquids, which is part of why it is called the universal solvent.

questions.topic: States of Water and Changes of State
questions.question: Which of these best describes what happens to the temperature of ice while it is melting at 0°C?
options: It stays at 0°C until all the ice has melted, even while heat is still being added
It rises steadily above 0°C throughout the melting process
It drops below 0°C during melting
Temperature has no relationship to melting
questions.explanation: While ice is melting at 0°C, its temperature stays at 0°C until all of the ice has changed to liquid, because the added heat energy is being used to change its state rather than raise its temperature.

questions.question: Which of these best explains why water is essential for regulating body temperature in humans and animals?
options: Sweating allows water to evaporate from skin, which cools the body down
Water always raises body temperature when it touches skin
Water has no effect on body temperature at all
Water only affects temperature when frozen
questions.explanation: Water helps regulate body temperature through sweating — as sweat (mostly water) evaporates from the skin, it carries away heat, cooling the body down.

questions.question: Which stage of the water cycle directly follows condensation, once cloud droplets become too heavy to stay suspended in the air?
options: Precipitation
Evaporation
Transpiration
Collection only, with no precipitation involved
questions.explanation: Once cloud droplets become too heavy to stay suspended in the air, they fall as precipitation (rain, snow, sleet, or hail), which directly follows condensation.

questions.question: Which of these best explains why powdered sugar generally dissolves faster in water than a single large sugar cube of the same total mass?
options: Powdered sugar has much more surface area exposed to the water, allowing faster interaction
Powdered sugar is a completely different substance from sugar cubes
Sugar cubes always dissolve faster than powdered sugar
Surface area has no effect on dissolving speed
questions.explanation: Powdered sugar has much more surface area exposed to water compared to a solid cube of the same mass, allowing it to interact with and dissolve into water faster.

questions.topic: States of Water and Changes of State
questions.question: Which of these best describes 'condensation' as a change of state?
options: Gas changing into liquid
Liquid changing into gas
Solid changing into liquid
Liquid changing into solid
questions.explanation: Condensation is the change of state from gas (water vapour) into liquid (water droplets), such as when water vapour cools and forms clouds or dew.

questions.question: Which of these best describes 'clarity' or 'transparency' as a physical property of pure water?
options: Light can pass through it, allowing objects to be seen clearly through it
It always blocks all light completely
It changes colour depending on the container
It becomes opaque as soon as it is poured
questions.explanation: Pure water's transparency means light can pass through it, allowing objects to be seen clearly through the water, which is a key physical property.

questions.question: Which of these is the best description of 'collection' as a stage of the water cycle?
options: Water gathering in oceans, rivers, lakes, and groundwater after falling as precipitation
Water vapour rising into the atmosphere
Water vapour turning into clouds
Water changing directly from solid to gas
questions.explanation: Collection is the stage where water that has fallen as precipitation gathers in oceans, rivers, lakes, and groundwater, ready to continue the water cycle.

questions.question: Water can act as a solvent for gases as well as solids, such as dissolved oxygen supporting fish in a river.
questions.explanation: Water can dissolve gases as well as solids — dissolved oxygen in rivers and lakes, for example, is essential for supporting fish and other aquatic life.

questions.question: A weather scientist notices that a nearby lake's water level has stayed almost the same all year, despite regular evaporation. What best explains this balance?
options: Precipitation and inflow from rivers/groundwater are roughly balancing the water lost to evaporation over the year
The lake never loses any water to evaporation
Evaporation from the lake has stopped completely
Water levels always decrease steadily with no possibility of balance
questions.explanation: A stable lake level despite evaporation suggests that precipitation and inflow from rivers or groundwater are roughly balancing the water being lost to evaporation over the year.

questions.topic: States of Water and Changes of State
questions.question: Which of these best summarizes water's three states, in order from most tightly packed/fixed shape to most freely moving/no fixed shape?
options: Solid (ice) → Liquid (water) → Gas (water vapour)
Gas → Liquid → Solid
Liquid → Solid → Gas
Gas → Solid → Liquid
questions.explanation: Water's three states, ordered from most tightly packed and fixed in shape to most freely moving with no fixed shape, are: solid (ice), liquid (water), and gas (water vapour).
